findings.title: 0331 newly ADMITS contract_confirmation on the accrual machine lane, which no ticket asked for and #1051 lists out of scope
findings.evidence: #1080's Out of scope: "Widening or narrowing the authority-reference vocabulary itself." #1051's Out of scope: "admitting `contract_confirmation` on the OBO lane." Before 0331, clara._accrual_plan_core carried 0222/0283's own two-kind list ('accounting_work','chat_task') at 0283:621-712; 0331 replaces it with `perform clara._assert_plan_authority(...)` (0331_accrual_plan_authority_wall.sql:212), and that predicate admits THREE kinds (0330_plan_authority_wall_predicate.sql:178). Measured on clara_l04: clara._assert_plan_authority is now called by exactly {_accrual_plan_core, _obo_plan_core, create_accounting_plan}. The ticket report names this itself ("What moves, beyond the refusal the ticket is about", row 2) and argues parity. The mitigation checks out: I re-measured the only two writers of clara.contract_plan_confirmations (confirm_tenancy_rent_plan, confirm_tenancy_rent_plan_revision) and both are granted to clara_authenticated alone, so clara_runtime cannot manufacture the row; and the HUMAN accrual door has admitted the kind since 0222 (it nests create_accounting_plan). But it is still an authority wall on a machine-only door (clara.create_accrual_adjustment_for, clara_runtime only) admitting a kind it refused before, against the standing owner ruling that access control is never loosened.
findings.required_fix: Integrator or owner records explicit acceptance of the accrual OBO lane admitting contract_confirmation before release; otherwise take the parameterised admitted set #1051's own brief anticipates ("the shared predicate takes a parameter, not a second copy") and keep the accrual machine lane at two kinds.

findings.title: #1051 AC3 is not satisfied on the branch as it stands: the from-scratch chain was never run, and plain `CI=true GITHUB_ACTIONS=true pnpm lint` is red
findings.evidence: #1051 AC3 verbatim: "From-scratch chain green; `CI=true GITHUB_ACTIONS=true pnpm lint` exit 0." The report marks it DONE/partial: the from-scratch chain is deliberately not runnable in-lane (RIG.md forbids a second from-scratch chain on a lane cluster) and is deferred to the integrator. I re-ran the lint's first step on the branch: `CI=true GITHUB_ACTIONS=true node scripts/check-frozen-workflows.mjs` reports 38 violations (REMOVED-VS-BASE chatTurn.v22.*, claraWork.v6.*, statementFacts.v4.*, UNLOCKED-VS-BASE payrollFacts.v1.*, three REGISTRY-DOWNGRADE lines). Cause is base drift, not the lane: origin/main has moved to 3bf6aa94d (the cut phase, PR #1142) while this lane's base is 7bc5a710f, and the lane's diff touches no packages/runtime file. With FREEZE_BASE_REF=7bc5a710f the chain is exit 0, as #1073/#1075/#1070's reports record. So #1051's own "exit 0, run twice" was true when measured and is no longer reproducible as the AC words it.
findings.required_fix: Wave-level decision at integration: either rebase the sweep lanes onto the merged cut head, or run the freeze lint with FREEZE_BASE_REF set to the wave base and say so in the integration record. Run the true from-scratch chain on a disposable cluster before #1051 is closed.

findings.title: #1075 AC2 is deferred and nothing carries the obligation forward: the new p_side parameter has zero callers
findings.evidence: #1075 AC2 verbatim: "The register's side filter control uses the server-side parameter once pagination exists, rather than filtering a fully-read page client-side." The deferral is defensible - the AC is conditional on pagination and the ticket's Out of scope says "Building pagination itself; this ticket only prepares the read for it. If pagination is not planned soon, this can wait until it is." Verified on the branch: apps/web/lib/accruals/api.ts `loadAccruals` still sends exactly {p_client, p_from, p_to} (api.ts:252-256) and apps/web/components/accruals/accruals-list.tsx still narrows the fully-read array client-side. So 0334 ships a parameter with no production caller, and the AC2 obligation lives only in the ticket report's prose.
findings.required_fix: Before #1075 is closed, either file the pagination follow-up that explicitly owns AC2 and link it on the ticket, or leave #1075 open with AC2 unticked. Do not close the ticket on AC1 alone.

findings.title: L1 edited CONTEXT.md four times although the plan of record assigns that file to L3 only
findings.evidence: SWEEP-PLAN.md's Shared files table: "CONTEXT.md | L3, only if #1049 stays in the wave". This lane edited it under #1051 (commit 2ada717aa, "Authorising instruction"), #1080 (f762c1a87, same paragraph), #1074 (ab42ceb55, "Plan occurrence" / "Accrual reversal" / "Accrual correction") and #1073 (fc9d61b2b, "Settlement candidate row"). Reviewed the diff: every hunk corrects a sentence the lane's own change made untrue (the entry still enumerated TWO authorising-instruction kinds; the conflict row still said "only two remedies" and "they both refuse"), no new term is minted, no new heading is added, and the four regions are disjoint. Each worker flagged the deviation in its own report.
findings.required_fix: Merger reconciles the four L1 regions against any L3 hunk; no code change proposed. If the plan's ownership rule is to hold, record the exception rather than leaving CONTEXT.md stating things the lane has made false.

findings.title: The on-screen hint states an unconditional ledger equivalence that holds only because a configuration wall elsewhere makes the counter-example unreachable
findings.evidence: apps/web/messages/en.json, new key accrualBillConflictReversePeriodHint: "It leaves the same amount on the books for this period as Reverse now does." The equality is driven (p1073.one_period.nets_like_reverse_now, re-run green), but the worker's own report withdrew a wider claim after measuring it: "reverse now" is a catch-up over [dueDate, _plan_reversal_date(dueDate)] and could admit a second event, and the only thing that stops it today is clara._assert_plan_schedule's reversal_collides_with_next_occurrence refusal (0193:1611) forbidding monthly/day_of_month=1 reversing plans. The sentence a bookkeeper reads carries no such condition, and the report itself files this as follow-up 2.
findings.required_fix: Owner judgement: keep the sentence (true of every schedule the estate admits today) or soften it to name the period rather than promise equivalence. Flagged so the claim is a decision rather than an accident.

findings.title: 0332 introduces a reversal that can refuse at posting time when a correction moved the accrual off an account that has since been deactivated
findings.evidence: The ticket asks only that "a reversal for an already-posted occurrence should reverse the amount that occurrence actually posted". 0332 achieves that by taking the POSTED entry's own lines (clara._plan_posted_entry_lines), which also fixes the account pair to the original one. The report's own "What moves" table, row 2: before 0332 the reversal posted to the NEW accounts (succeeded, stranded the balance); after 0332 "if one has since been deactivated it REFUSES at posting time through clara._validate_entry_lines's existing ... floor". No new refusal is minted, and the estate has no chart-account deactivation door today (SWEEP-PLAN's #1078 ruling calls account_inactive "a known harmless dead axis for chart accounts"), so the path is latent. It is correct accounting; it is also a hard stop with no named operator remedy.
findings.required_fix: None now. Record it so that whichever ticket ever opens chart-account deactivation owns the remedy for a posted period whose original account is gone.

findings.title: A web cell still mocks a refusal sentence that 0331's own tail asserts exists nowhere in the estate
findings.evidence: apps/web/components/accruals/accrual-form.test.tsx:336-345 (652.form: a form-level refusal is a persistent banner carrying the code and reason) throws refusal("CLR10", "authority_ref_unresolved", "the instruction this accrual cites does not exist for this client"). Grepped the migrations: the sentence survives only in the applied 0222:1022 and 0283:662 pre-images and inside 0331's own pin constants and tail message (0331:298, 0331:396), and 0331's T.4d asserts ZERO live clara bodies carry it. The cell passes because the value is mocked, and the door the form actually calls (clara.create_accrual_adjustment via api.ts) has answered the *plan* sentence since 0222. Pre-existing staleness that 0331 turns from "wrong door" into "nonexistent string"; the worker named it as follow-up 1 and deliberately left apps/web untouched.
findings.required_fix: One-line string fix in whichever lane next touches accrual-form.test.tsx, or a follow-up ticket. Not a blocker for this wave.

findings.title: The per-period schedule is rendered as the page's own read-only table, not "in the same shape the form's own block uses"
findings.evidence: #1070 Desired behavior: "the per-period stated amounts as a schedule (due date and amount, in the same shape the form's own block uses)". accrual-detail.tsx renders a DataTableCard/Table with colDue/colAmount rather than mounting AccrualPeriodAmountsBlock. The worker's reason is sound and recorded: that block is a select/input/remove-button editor with no read-only mode, and a detail view should not offer a control whose only outcome is editing an admitted row. The message key periodAmountsHeading IS the form's own and formatCents is the same formatter, so the labelling half of the requirement is met.
